title: Ledger Flex from Metapod, Singapore airport

implant.notes: The buyer never plugged the device in. They noticed scratches on the casing and sent it to @MagicalTux for teardown, which found an added flex PCB with an antenna lead on the back cover and a separate implant PCB.

sources.author: Ben Yorke
sources.text:
I have a $300 @Ledger Flex that I bought from the Singapore airport in summer (Metapod, should be fine?)

I never plugged it in but it looks like theres some scratches on the casing, an indication of potential tampering?

Anyways theres no way i can trust it (or Ledger) now

sources.author: Mark Karpelès
sources.text:
Ledger Flex sold at Singapore Airport confirmed to contain a spy implant!
@BenYorke found suspicious marks on his @Ledger and sent it to me rather than using it, that was probably the best decision here.

sources.title: Spy implant found in Ledger Flex bought at Singapore airport
sources.author: Mark Karpeles

images.caption: The buyer's photo: a scratch on the casing edge (red box), photographed on the retail box.
Close-up of damage at the seam between the casing and the back cover.
Opened device. The back cover carries the added flex marked "AC-A2201-FLEX-欧亚版-V1.2", with an antenna lead running to the device.
Implant PCB after removal: STM32U575 MCU, a large module, and a u.FL antenna connector.
